paper_title: Mechanistic Understanding and Mitigation of Language Confusion in   English-Centric Large Language Models
caption: Distribution of Important Neurons Associated with Confusion Points in Llama3-8B. (a) Distribution of the top 300 most important FFN neurons across layers for an individual Chinese prompt “UTF8gbsn请解释拆东墙补西墙的意思。(Please explain `UTF8gbsn拆东墙补西墙.')” from Aya. (b) Aggregated distribution of important neuron scores across all Chinese test samples in Aya.

model_annotations.German:
The first plot, titled "(a) Individual Case," illustrates the count of Llama3 FFN value neurons across different layers. The x-axis is labeled "layer" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 32, with numeric tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "count," also on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 100 with tick labels every 20 units. A single solid blue line with circular markers represents the "Llama3 FFN value neurons." The line begins at layer 1 with a count near 0 and maintains a steady, low trend near 0 until layer 21. Minor fluctuations occur between layer 22 and layer 27, reaching a small peak of approximately 18 at layer 26 before dropping to roughly 6 at layer 27. The line then exhibits a steep upward trend, rising from roughly 18 at layer 28 to 25 at layer 29, approximately 78 at layer 30, and culminating in a peak of nearly 100 at the final data point at layer 31.

The second plot, titled "(b) Aggregated Neuron Scores," represents the aggregated count of Llama3 FFN value neurons across layers. The x-axis is labeled "layer" and features a linear scale ranging from 0 to 35, with numeric tick marks spaced by intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "count," uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 175, with numeric tick marks at intervals of 25. The plot contains a single solid green line with circular markers denoting the "Llama3 FFN value neurons." This line starts at layer 13 with a count near 0 and remains relatively flat and steady near 0 through layer 27. A sharp increase begins at layer 28, where the count is approximately 5, climbing to roughly 18 at layer 29, approximately 56 at layer 30, and reaching its highest peak of 175 at the final point at layer 31.
